cues.en: Another great analysis technique to have in your toolkit is called effective dimensionality.
cues.zh: 另一種很值得放進分析工具箱的技巧，叫作有效維度。

cues.en: It's very similar to compression and dimension reduction, and provides some insights into the nature of the shape of the data space inside the model.
cues.zh: 它與壓縮及降維很相似，能幫助我們了解模型內部資料空間形狀的性質。

cues.en: That's important because the information that the model can process is limited by the dimensionality of the data space.
cues.zh: 這很重要，因為模型能處理的資訊，受限於資料空間的維度。

cues.en: As a very simple example, imagine that the only dimension you could use to describe the conditions outside was temperature.
cues.zh: 舉個非常簡單的例子，假設你只能用溫度這一個維度，描述外面的狀況。

cues.en: Now, temperature certainly is an informative metric, but it's not everything.
cues.zh: 溫度當然是有資訊價值的指標，但並非一切。

cues.en: If you have the humidity as well, then that tells you a lot more information about what it's like outside.
cues.zh: 如果還有濕度，就能對外面的狀況提供更多資訊。

cues.en: So temperature and humidity would mean two dimensions of information.
cues.zh: 所以溫度與濕度，代表兩個資訊維度。

cues.en: And then perhaps cloud coverage would be a third dimension.
cues.zh: 雲量或許可以是第三個維度。

cues.en: So the more dimensions the information is represented and processed in, the more contextual details the model can represent and calculate.
cues.zh: 資訊被表徵與處理的維度越多，模型就能表徵與計算更多上下文細節。

cues.en: Now, the precise interpretation of dimensionality here gets pretty tricky because there are so many nonlinear transformations throughout the model.
cues.zh: 不過，這裡維度的精確解讀相當棘手，因為整個模型有許多非線性轉換。

cues.en: And every linear transformation inside the model is both preceded and followed by a nonlinear transformation.
cues.zh: 模型內的每項線性轉換，前後都有非線性轉換。

cues.en: Nonetheless, effective dimensionality is still pretty interesting and I think can be quite useful in mech interp analyses.
cues.zh: 儘管如此，有效維度仍相當有意思，我覺得對機制可解釋性分析很有用。

cues.en: So let me begin with a reminder about principal components analysis.
cues.zh: 先複習主成分分析、

cues.en: The singular value decomposition and percent variance explained.
cues.zh: 奇異值分解，以及解釋變異百分比。

cues.en: Actually, if you are unfamiliar with SVD, then I recommend going back to this video from earlier in the course to get a refresher.
cues.zh: 如果不熟悉 SVD，我建議回頭看課程前面的這支影片，複習一下。

cues.en: You do not need to watch the entire video, just the beginning part of the lecture where I provided
cues.zh: 不需要看完整支，只要看課程一開始，

cues.en: a high level intro to the singular value decomposition briefly and as a reminder of the reminder.
cues.zh: 我概略介紹奇異值分解的部分。再簡短複習一下這個複習。

cues.en: The idea is that we have a data set stored as a two dimensional matrix.
cues.zh: 概念是，把資料集存成一個二維矩陣，

cues.en: So rows and columns.
cues.zh: 也就是有列與欄。

cues.en: And then we take the SVD of that matrix.
cues.zh: 接著對這個矩陣做 SVD，

cues.en: And we get the singular values and singular vectors.
cues.zh: 取得奇異值與奇異向量。

cues.en: Now earlier in the course we were actually using these singular vectors.
cues.zh: 課程前面，其實會使用這些奇異向量。

cues.en: But now here in this video and also in the next video, we don't actually care about the vectors per se.
cues.zh: 但這支與下一支影片，並不在意向量本身，

cues.en: We're really just going to focus on the singular values for the analyses.
cues.zh: 分析主要只專注於奇異值。

cues.en: The singular values encode the importance of each direction in the data, and importance in the context
cues.zh: 奇異值編碼資料中各個方向的重要性，而在 PCA 的脈絡中，重要性

cues.en: of PCA is the amount of variance along that direction.
cues.zh: 就是沿著該方向的變異量。

cues.en: So, for example, in this data set, PCA would identify this line as the most important direction in
cues.zh: 例如，在這份資料中，PCA 會將這條線辨識為資料中最重要的

cues.en: the data, because the most amount of variance in the data aligns with this vector with this direction.
cues.zh: 方向，因為資料中最大量的變異，沿著這個向量、這個方向排列。

cues.en: So this vector, this direction here would have a large singular value.
cues.zh: 所以這個向量、這個方向，會有較大的奇異值。

cues.en: The next most important direction in this data would be this one.
cues.zh: 這份資料中，第二重要的方向則是這個，

cues.en: And its singular value will be smaller.
cues.zh: 它的奇異值會比較小。

cues.en: Now we can plot all of the singular values in a plot, and that would look something like this.
cues.zh: 我們可以將所有奇異值畫成圖，大概會像這樣。

cues.en: This kind of plot is variously called the SVD spectrum, the singular value spectrum, or the scree plot, or something like that.
cues.zh: 這種圖有不同名稱，例如 SVD 譜、奇異值譜、陡坡圖等等。

cues.en: Now here's the cool thing about singular values.
cues.zh: 奇異值有個很酷的特性。

cues.en: All of the singular vectors have unit norm, which means a magnitude of one.
cues.zh: 所有奇異向量都是單位範數，也就是大小為 1。

cues.en: And that means that the vectors themselves do not actually contain any information other than direction.
cues.zh: 這表示向量本身，除了方向之外，其實不包含任何其他資訊。

cues.en: In other words, all of the variability in the data.
cues.zh: 換句話說，資料中的所有變異，

cues.en: So all the variance, all the covariance across all the variables, it's all stored in the singular values.
cues.zh: 也就是所有變異數、所有變數之間的所有共變異數，全部儲存在奇異值裡。

cues.en: And technically it's the squared singular values because of the relationship between singular values and eigenvalues of the data matrix transpose.
cues.zh: 嚴格來說，是奇異值的平方，因為奇異值與資料矩陣轉置的特徵值之間有這種關係。

cues.en: If you've taken a course on linear algebra, then that statement should sound familiar.
cues.zh: 如果修過線性代數，這句話應該很熟悉。

cues.en: And if not, then don't worry about it.
cues.zh: 如果沒有，也別擔心。

cues.en: The point is that 100% of the variability in the data is stored in the collection of singular values,
cues.zh: 重點是，資料 100% 的變異，都儲存在這組奇異值中，

cues.en: and therefore we can calculate how much variability is stored in each component or each direction using this formula.
cues.zh: 因此能透過這個公式，計算每個成分、每個方向儲存多少變異。

cues.en: Here, where r squared is a general statistical term used to indicate the proportion of variance explained,
cues.zh: 這裡的 R 平方，是表示解釋變異比例的一般統計用語，

cues.en: and the sigmas are the singular values.
cues.zh: 而 sigma 是奇異值。

cues.en: So square all of the singular values, sum them all up, and then divide that into each of the individual singular values.
cues.zh: 將所有奇異值平方後加總，再用這個總和去除各個奇異值。

cues.en: That gives you the proportion of variance accounted for by each principal component.
cues.zh: 這就得到各主成分所解釋的變異比例。

cues.en: And you can multiply this by 100 to get the percent variance explained.
cues.zh: 再乘以 100，就是解釋變異百分比。

cues.en: So that's all fine.
cues.zh: 這些都沒問題，

cues.en: But how do we get to effective dimensionality.
cues.zh: 但要如何得到有效維度？

cues.en: In fact the dimensionality of the data space is kind of trivial.
cues.zh: 其實資料空間的維度有點簡單，

cues.en: It's simply the number of tokens that you have in the sequence or the number of neurons in the layer.
cues.zh: 就是序列中的 token 數，或該層中的神經元數，

cues.en: Whichever of those two is smaller.
cues.zh: 取兩者較小者。

cues.en: But that is the mathematical definition of the ambient dimensionality.
cues.zh: 但那是環境維度的數學定義。

cues.en: The effective dimensionality is actually determined by the data, not by the number of columns in the matrix.
cues.zh: 有效維度其實由資料本身決定，而不是矩陣的欄數。

cues.en: And I'd like to give you an example to help you understand this concept of effective dimensionality.
cues.zh: 我想先舉個例子，幫助你理解有效維度這個概念，

cues.en: And then I'll get into the math.
cues.zh: 再談數學。

cues.en: So think about a piece of paper.
cues.zh: 想像一張紙。

cues.en: Technically this piece of paper is three dimensional.
cues.zh: 嚴格來說，這張紙是三維的，

cues.en: But one of the dimensions is so thin that it cannot be used for any practical purpose.
cues.zh: 但其中一個維度薄到沒有任何實際用途。

cues.en: So we really only use a piece of paper as a two dimensional object.
cues.zh: 因此我們實際上，只把紙當成二維物件使用。

cues.en: Of course, physically it exists in three dimensions.
cues.zh: 當然，物理上它存在於三維空間，

cues.en: But effectively the thickness dimension is so thin that it has no application value.
cues.zh: 但實質上，厚度這個維度太薄，沒有應用價值。

cues.en: So we can say that a piece of paper has an effective dimensionality of two.
cues.zh: 所以可以說，紙的有效維度是 2。

cues.en: Here are some examples with data.
cues.zh: 這裡有一些資料的例子。

cues.en: Let's first look at this one on the left.
cues.zh: 先看左邊這個。

cues.en: These data live in two dimensions.
cues.zh: 這些資料位於二維空間，

cues.en: There are two axes, but all of the data points sit on a line.
cues.zh: 有兩個軸，但全部資料點都位於一條直線上。

cues.en: So although the ambient dimensionality is two, the data really live in a one dimensional subspace.
cues.zh: 所以雖然環境維度是 2，資料實際上位於一維子空間。

cues.en: So we can say that the effective dimensionality is one, although technically the true dimensionality is two.
cues.zh: 因此可以說，有效維度是 1，雖然嚴格來說，真正的維度是 2。

cues.en: Now how about this one over here?
cues.zh: 那麼這邊這個呢？

cues.en: Certainly these data are strongly correlated.
cues.zh: 這些資料當然高度相關。

cues.en: Would you say that the effective dimensionality here is 1 or 2?
cues.zh: 你會說有效維度是 1，還是 2？

cues.en: It's not really clear what the answer should be, because it depends on what you think of the variability off of the diagonal.
cues.zh: 答案其實不明確，因為取決於你如何看待偏離對角線的變異。

cues.en: Is this noise or is this important meaningful variability?
cues.zh: 那是雜訊，還是重要、有意義的變異？

cues.en: We could compress the data down to one dimension and then say that everything off the perfect diagonal is noise.
cues.zh: 可以將資料壓縮成一維，再把偏離完美對角線的一切都視為雜訊，

cues.en: We don't think it carries any meaningful information that we want to preserve in the analysis.
cues.zh: 認為它們不包含分析中想要保留的任何有意義資訊。

cues.en: And that is basically how compression by dimension reduction works.
cues.zh: 這基本上就是透過降維進行壓縮的方式。

cues.en: So let's say we have some threshold, and we say that the variability on this smaller axis is considered
cues.zh: 假設有個門檻，我們說，沿這條較小軸的變異，若小於

cues.en: noise if it's smaller than some amount, and we consider it meaningful and we do not want to compress it out.
cues.zh: 某個量，就視為雜訊；若較大，就視為有意義，不希望壓縮掉它，

cues.en: If it's bigger than that threshold.
cues.zh: 也就是大於該門檻時。

cues.en: And what do we take as a threshold in the context of PCA and the SVD, we can take the percent of total data variability as a threshold.
cues.zh: 那門檻要選什麼？在 PCA 與 SVD 的脈絡中，可以用資料總變異的百分比作為門檻。

cues.en: So what you see in these plots here are the singular value spectrum of a data matrix converted to percent
cues.zh: 這些圖顯示資料矩陣的奇異值譜，並使用上一張投影片的公式，轉成解釋變異

cues.en: variance, using the formula that I showed in the previous slide.
cues.zh: 百分比。

cues.en: And this is the kind of pattern that you see very often in all sorts of data in biological systems and physical systems and so on.
cues.zh: 在生物系統、物理系統等各種資料中，經常看到這種模式。

cues.en: The first couple of components tend to account for a relatively large amount of variability.
cues.zh: 前幾個成分，往往能解釋相對大量的變異，

cues.en: And then that goes down.
cues.zh: 接著逐漸下降。

cues.en: And the other components account for a relatively small amount of variability.
cues.zh: 其他成分，只解釋相對少量的變異。

cues.en: And what you see over here is exactly the same data.
cues.zh: 這裡看到的是完全相同的資料，

cues.en: But now it's the cumulative sum.
cues.zh: 但改成累加總和。

cues.en: So the first point down here is equal to this point over here it's around 25.
cues.zh: 所以，下面第一個點等於這裡這個點，大約是 25。

cues.en: And then the second point here is around 40.
cues.zh: 第二個點大約是 40，

cues.en: That is the cumulative sum of the first two points here.
cues.zh: 也就是這裡前兩個點的累加總和，

cues.en: So 25 plus 15 and so on.
cues.zh: 25 加 15，依此類推。

cues.en: So the interpretation of this cumulative variance explained plot is that, for example, if you take
cues.zh: 所以這張累積解釋變異圖的解讀是，例如取

cues.en: the first 20 components, then that together all first 20 components together accounts for around 70%
cues.zh: 前 20 個成分，這前 20 個成分加在一起，就能解釋大約 70%，

cues.en: of the total variability of the data set.
cues.zh: 也就是資料集總變異的 70%。

cues.en: So now we can pick some threshold, let's say 80%.
cues.zh: 現在可以挑一個門檻，例如 80%。

cues.en: And we can ask how many components in the data or in the PCA of the data does it take to account for
cues.zh: 接著問，資料中，或者說資料 PCA 中，要多少個成分，才能解釋

cues.en: 80% of the variance of the entire data set?
cues.zh: 整份資料集 80% 的變異？

cues.en: And that is the number that we take to be the effective dimensionality.
cues.zh: 我們就將這個數字，當作有效維度。

cues.en: So let's say there are 100 components in total.
cues.zh: 假設總共有 100 個成分。

cues.en: In this case we would say the effective dimensionality is around 55.
cues.zh: 這裡就會說，有效維度大約是 55。

cues.en: Now we cannot actually visualize a 100 dimensional space.
cues.zh: 我們當然無法真正將一個 100 維空間視覺化，

cues.en: But the interpretation would be the same as this piece of paper.
cues.zh: 但解讀方式與那張紙相同。

cues.en: So inside the LM there is a 100 dimensional space.
cues.zh: 也就是語言模型內有一個 100 維空間，

cues.en: But all of the token embeddings are actually only really occupying 55 of those dimensions.
cues.zh: 但所有 token 嵌入，實際上只真正占據其中 55 個維度。

cues.en: The other 45 dimensions are kind of like the width of the paper.
cues.zh: 其他 45 個維度，就有點像紙的寬度。

cues.en: Now to be clear, a cumulative percent variance explained threshold of 80 is way too low.
cues.zh: 不過要說清楚，累積解釋變異百分比門檻設為 80，實在太低。

cues.en: Normally you would use 95 or 99%, maybe 99.9% of the variance.
cues.zh: 一般會用 95%、99%，或甚至 99.9% 的變異。

cues.en: But for illustration purposes, I didn't feel like going out to all of the 1000 components that are
cues.zh: 但為了示範，我不想一路畫到這份資料集實際上

cues.en: actually in this dataset, just because I wanted to visualize this descent over here to the left.
cues.zh: 包含的 1,000 個成分，因為只是想呈現左邊這個下降趨勢。

cues.en: So I'm just drawing these lines at 80, just to give you a visual intuition of the analysis.
cues.zh: 所以才把線畫在 80，只是提供分析的視覺直覺。

cues.en: And you will see how this actually looks when I switch to code in a few minutes.
cues.zh: 幾分鐘後切換到程式碼，就會看到實際的樣子。

cues.en: And also just to be clear about the interpretation.
cues.zh: 關於解讀，也再說清楚一點。

cues.en: All of the dimensions are technically mathematically present, but there's such a tiny amount of variability
cues.zh: 嚴格從數學來看，所有維度都存在，但後面這些成分中的變異

cues.en: in these later components that we consider it to be noise or unimportant.
cues.zh: 實在太少，所以將它們視為雜訊或不重要。

cues.en: Of course, that is a huge assumption, and it is certainly very possible that tiny amounts of variance
cues.zh: 當然，這是很大的假設，而且完全有可能，在正確維度、

cues.en: in just the right dimensions, in just the right neurons are actually really important for guiding the model forwards.
cues.zh: 正確神經元中，一點點變異，其實對引導模型往前運作非常重要。

cues.en: Nonetheless, you can run this kind of analysis and then compare the results for different layers or
cues.zh: 儘管如此，仍然可以做這種分析，再比較不同層、

cues.en: different data sets, different token types or categories, different parts of speech, different context, windows, etc., etc. it's quite a versatile method.
cues.zh: 不同資料集、不同 token 類型或類別、不同詞性、不同上下文視窗等等的結果。它的用途相當靈活。

cues.en: And even though there are some arbitrary features like what number to use as a threshold, the overall
cues.zh: 即使有些特徵是任意選擇的，例如門檻要用什麼數字，

cues.en: patterns are going to be pretty similar when you compare for different categories or different layers.
cues.zh: 比較不同類別或不同層時，整體模式還是會很相似。

cues.en: So in the Python demo, in this video I will show you how to write and use and run the code to generate these kinds of analyses.
cues.zh: 這支影片的 Python 示範，會展示如何編寫、使用與執行這些分析程式。

cues.en: And then in the code challenge in the next video, you are going to adapt and expand these methods to
cues.zh: 接著，下一支影片的程式挑戰，要請你調整並擴充這些方法，

cues.en: a much bigger model, to more layers and to a couple of different data sets.
cues.zh: 用到大得多的模型、更多層，以及幾份不同的資料集。

cues.en: So here's what we're going to do in the Python demo.
cues.zh: 以下是 Python 示範的內容。

cues.en: I'll start by importing GPT two XL.
cues.zh: 先匯入 GPT2-XL。

cues.en: You have seen this model before.
cues.zh: 以前已經看過這個模型。

cues.en: It has 48 transformer blocks and an embeddings dimensionality of 1600.
cues.zh: 它有 48 個 Transformer 區塊，嵌入維度是 1,600。

cues.en: And that is great because it means that when we set up the effective dimensionality analysis, we can
cues.zh: 這很好，因為設定好有效維度分析後，

cues.en: apply it to every single layer in exactly the same way, with exactly the same parameters and thresholds.
cues.zh: 就能用完全相同的方式、完全相同的參數與門檻，套用到每一層。

cues.en: The tokens I will use to process the data and get the activations are from the book through the Looking glass, which we've used several times before in this course.
cues.zh: 用來處理資料、取得活化的 token，來自課程中用過好幾次的《鏡中奇緣》。

cues.en: And as a reference, what I'm going to do is completely scramble all of these tokens.
cues.zh: 作為參考，我會將所有這些 token 完全打亂。

cues.en: So it's exactly the same tokens in both analyses, but just with different orderings.
cues.zh: 因此兩種分析使用完全相同的 token，只是順序不同。

cues.en: So that's a pretty interesting comparison, because any difference that we observe in effective dimensionality
cues.zh: 這是很有意思的比較，因為觀察到的任何有效維度差異，

cues.en: cannot be attributable to the tokens themselves, but instead are entirely attributable to the order in which the tokens appear.
cues.zh: 都不能歸因於 token 本身，而完全來自 token 出現的順序。

cues.en: Now for this analysis we will use the hidden state activations.
cues.zh: 這次分析使用隱藏狀態活化。

cues.en: We're not using any hooks.
cues.zh: 不會使用任何 hook。

cues.en: You know how to do that yourself if you want to follow up on those kinds of analyses.

cues.zh: 後面的 Transformer 區塊，才開始出現真正的區別，打亂 token 實際占據的子空間稍小，

cues.en: And the real tokens are occupying a larger space.
cues.zh: 真實 token 則占據較大的空間。

cues.en: And why does this generally get bigger?
cues.zh: 那麼，為什麼整體會變大？

cues.en: Remember that as we get deeper into the model, the model is learning to incorporate more and more context
cues.zh: 記住，隨著模型越來越深，模型會在目前 token 的處理中，納入越來越多

cues.en: into the processing of the current token in order to transform it into a next token.
cues.zh: 上下文，才能將它轉換成下一個 token。

cues.en: So that is pretty difficult to do, and therefore the complexity of the representations and the calculations Populations increases.
cues.zh: 這件事相當困難，因此表徵與計算的複雜性會增加。

cues.en: And so the model needs to basically expand the effective dimensionality of the analysis here.

cues.en: Once you get the concept of this analysis approach you can apply it to lots of different data sets.
cues.zh: 掌握這種分析方法的概念後，就能套用到很多不同資料集。

cues.en: And now the exact numerical results will depend on the threshold, which itself is a bit arbitrary.
cues.zh: 精確數值結果會取決於門檻，而門檻本身有點任意。

cues.en: You know why use 95% variance explained as a threshold?
cues.zh: 為什麼要用 95% 解釋變異作為門檻？

cues.en: Why not 94%?
cues.zh: 為什麼不是 94%？

cues.en: Or how about 98.327%?
So it is a good idea to explore different thresholds and interpret relative dimensionalities and not the exact number.
cues.zh: 所以最好探索不同門檻，解讀相對維度，而不是精確的數字。

cues.en: Also, keep in mind that there really are no linear calculations inside a deep learning model as big as an LN inside the model.
cues.zh: 也要記住，在像語言模型這麼大的深度學習模型內部，其實沒有真正的線性計算。

cues.en: Every linear calculation like dot product, for example, has a nonlinear transform before it and after it.
cues.zh: 每個線性計算，例如內積，前後都有非線性轉換。

cues.en: So there are like slices of linearity, but those are sandwiched in between non-linearities.
cues.zh: 所以雖然有一片片線性區段，但它們夾在非線性之間。

cues.en: So I am a huge fan of using linear analysis methods.
cues.zh: 我非常喜歡使用線性分析方法，

cues.en: They tend to be stable and robust and easier to interpret, but a compelling result of a linear analysis
cues.zh: 它們通常穩定、穩健，而且較容易解讀，但線性分析得到有說服力的結果，

cues.en: does not mean that the computation itself inside the model is linear.
cues.zh: 並不代表模型內部的計算本身就是線性的。
